title: Propheta's letters to Jim Garrison in the Garrison files
place_text: New Orleans, Louisiana; the Bronx, New York

tellings.quote: where the leader of the church, guy called Propheta, was writing letters to Jim Garrison saying, "When you're finished with Jack Martin, can you send him back to us?" Right.

plain: In the 1960s, the leader of a small church in the Bronx, a man called Propheta, wrote letters to Jim Garrison, the New Orleans district attorney who investigated the Kennedy assassination, asking about Jack Martin, a man caught up in that investigation. The author Peter Levenda tells Michels the letters sit in Garrison's correspondence files, and that Propheta wrote, "When you're finished with Jack Martin, can you send him back to us?" The letter as quoted shows Propheta claiming Martin as one of his own; what that tie meant, it does not say.
